subject: Cobalt Health - request for quarterly invoice cadence and extended payment terms
messages:
From: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@cobalthealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cobalthealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:13:05 -0700
Subject: Request: quarterly invoicing + extended payment window for first year

Hi Jonas / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks like a strong fit for our patient-facing features. Our procurement team needs a slightly different billing cadence to align with internal budgets: Cobalt wants quarterly invoices with payment on Net-90 for the first 12 months (our fiscal funding is quarterly and we don’t get approvals until close of quarter).

Key asks: 
- Quarterly invoices (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct) for the first year
- Net-90 on each invoice for the pilot year
- Standard T&Cs otherwise; we can sign an addendum if needed

I attached a term sheet from our procurement team that outlines the request (Cobalt_PO_TermSheet.pdf). We appreciate any flexibility here — this is a pilot we expect to expand quickly if the metrics look good.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate this and what, if any, commercial concessions would be required?

Thanks,
Oliver Stone
Director, Procurement
Cobalt Health

--
Attachment: Cobalt_PO_TermSheet.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver.stone@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:02:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: quarterly invoicing + extended payment window for first year

Oliver —

Appreciate the clear ask and the term sheet. We can consider a temporary cadence change for the pilot but there are two things to flag from our side: cash flow exposure for Redwood and accounting complexity if we push to Net-90 without compensating commercial terms.

Proposed compromise to move forward quickly (pending approvals):
- Redwood can agree to quarterly invoicing for the pilot year.
- Payments would be Net-60 by default; we can approve Net-90 for the first two invoices only if Cobalt accepts a 1.5% administrative fee per invoice and a 10% retention (holdback) that is released after payment clears for the next invoice.
- We will add an addendum to the MSA (one-page) documenting cadence, fees, and holdback.

I've put together a short mutual action plan (MAP_Cobalt.xlsx) showing milestones, billing dates, and the financial impact. Priyom and Vanessa are looped in for legal/finance sign-off. If you can confirm acceptance of the 1.5% fee + 10% holdback, I’ll escalate for final executive approval and send the addendum for signature.

Next steps: 
1) Oliver: confirm acceptance of fee + holdback (reply)
2) Redwood: internal approval -> finalize addendum -> sign

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales Director | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 08:37:48 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: quarterly invoicing + extended payment window for first year

Team —

I reviewed Oliver's term sheet and Jonas' proposed compromise. From a finance perspective the main risks are collection timing and AR concentration (pilot invoice could sit for 90 days). If we were to approve Net-90 we should require compensating controls:

- Limit Net-90 to the first two invoices (pilot only); revert to Net-60 thereafter
- 10% holdback per invoice until payment is confirmed
- A 1.5% administrative fee applies to each quarterly invoice to offset financing cost
- Require ACH pre-authorization or a credit card on file with 30% pre-authorization on the first invoice (helps mitigate initial exposure)

If the customer accepts those constraints I'm comfortable escalating to Marissa for exec approval. If they push for Net-90 for the full year, we should decline unless there is a prepay or significantly higher fee (3-4%).

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Marissa —

Forwarding for executive sign-off. Summary: Cobalt Health (pilot customer) requests quarterly invoicing + Net-90 for the pilot year. Sales proposes: quarterly invoices, Net-60 standard, Net-90 for first two invoices only if customer accepts 1.5% admin fee, 10% holdback, and ACH pre-auth / card on file. Finance (Vanessa) agrees to escalate with those constraints.

Attachments: MAP_Cobalt.xlsx and Cobalt_PO_TermSheet.pdf. I also drafted a one-page addendum summarizing the terms (approval_summary.pdf) — would appreciate a short yes/no or suggested edits so we can respond to procurement this week.

Why approve? This is a strategic pilot in a target vertical (healthcare) with expansion potential; losing momentum here would likely push procurement to an alternative vendor.

Risks: increased AR and administrative overhead. Proposed mitigations above.

Thanks for a quick take — we need a decision by 10/13 to keep their procurement cycle on track.

Team / Oliver,

After reviewing the addendum and the MAP: approved with conditions. Executive decision: make the exception for the pilot only, on the following terms that must be included in the addendum and signed before any invoice goes out.

Approval conditions (required):
1) Quarterly invoicing for pilot only (12 months).
2) Net-90 allowed for the first two quarterly invoices only. All subsequent invoices revert to Net-60.
3) 1.5% administrative fee applied to each quarterly invoice.
4) 10% holdback retained per invoice; holdback released after payment clears for the subsequent invoice.
5) ACH pre-authorization or credit card on file with a 30% pre-authorization on first invoice.
6) Finance to create a separate AR aging flag and weekly collection check-ins for the pilot.

Jonas, please get the customer to sign the addendum (attach to the amendment of the MSA). Priyom / Legal: confirm wording for holdback and fee. Vanessa: please coordinate AR flagging and update billing system. Aditya: coordinate implementation timeline with infra so we can map invoice dates to usage.

Marissa Cole
